parts.title: Multiple choice
parts.instructions: This examination paper has 50 multiple choice questions (1 to 50). Each question has 4 choices. Choose one best answer and blacken the letter of your choice on the separate answer sheet.

source.notes: Transcribed from the V-A text layer and checked against the page images; V-B OCR used to confirm wording. Bold-underlined emphasis words (is not, correct, was not, is true, does not, first, last, did not) are kept as <u>…</u>. Figure 1 (road between towns A and B), Figure 2 (classroom plan 3 cm × 2 cm) and Figure 3 (water-cycle drawings 1–4) were cropped from 300-dpi page renders. The visible cover gives 1 hour and 10 minutes (70 minutes); the text layer also contains a hidden leftover line '1 hour and 40 minutes (100 minutes)' that is not printed.
source.printing_note: Degree signs printed as 0 in Q7 (360E and 430E) – shown as °. Q7 option A has longitudes with N (36°N and 43°N), a real misprint in the options. Q8 'Masswa'. Q45 option D is followed by a stray '46.' (removed).

exam.answer_key_note: No official key. Answers solved and checked against the Eritrean MoE Grade 6–8 textbooks.

questions.stem: One of the following <u>is not</u> a highland crop.
explanation_steps: Wheat, barley and beans (pulses) are highland crops (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 132).
Sesame needs high temperature. It is a lowland crop (Grade 8, p. 8; Grade 6, p. 94). Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Sesame grows in the hot lowlands, not in the highlands.
tips: Highlands: wheat, barley, beans. Lowlands: sesame, sorghum.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a lowland crop?
explanation_steps: Sorghum needs heat. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 1 – Relief in Eritrea, Lowlands, p. 8
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Hatshepsut was the queen of:
explanation_steps: The textbook: in 1500 B.C. Queen Hatshepsut of Egypt sent ships to the land of Punt (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 60). Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Hatshepsut was a queen of Egypt.

similar_questions.stem: Queen Hatshepsut sent ships to:
explanation_steps: To Punt. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 8 – Eritrea 900 B.C.E–1300 C.E, The Land of Punt, p. 60
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: The earliest community that lived by hunting and gathering was:
explanation_steps: The textbook: at the time of early human development (Primitive Communal Society) people collected roots, fruits and eggs and hunted animals (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 79).
Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: The first people were hunters and gatherers in primitive communal society.
tips: First stage = primitive communal (hunting and gathering).

similar_questions.stem: Which stage came after primitive communal society?
explanation_steps: Slave society came next. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 6 – Government, 6.1 Development of Government, p. 79

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> a natural disaster?
explanation_steps: The textbook: natural disasters include earthquakes, floods, drought and volcanic eruption. Man-made disasters are war, pollution, deforestation, erosion (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 113).
Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: War is made by people. It is not natural.
tips: Natural = from nature. War = from people.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a natural disaster?
explanation_steps: A flood comes from nature. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 8 – Disasters in Eritrea, 8.1 What is Disaster?, p. 113

questions.stem: Relief describes:

options.A: The climate of the earth’s surface
options.B: The vegetation cover of the earth’s surface
options.C: The shape of the earth’s surface
options.D: The rocks of the earth’s surface

explanation_steps: The textbook: relief means the shape of the earth's surface (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 2). Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Relief is the shape of the land.

similar_questions.stem: Which one is a relief feature?
explanation_steps: A mountain is a shape of the land. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 1 – Relief in Eritrea, 1.1 What is Relief?, p. 2

questions.stem: Which of the following rivers flows to the east?
explanation_steps: The textbook: Mereb, Barka and Anseba flow into the Sudan (west). The rivers that flow to the Red Sea (east) include Felket, Laba, Labka, Hadas and Alighede (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 18).
Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: The Hadas flows east to the Red Sea.
tips: East to Red Sea: Hadas. West to Sudan: Mereb, Barka, Anseba.

similar_questions.stem: Which river flows west into the Sudan?
explanation_steps: Barka. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Eritrea is located between longitudes of _________ and ________.
explanation_steps: The textbook: Eritrea's longitudinal location is between 36° East and 43° East; its latitude is between 12° North and 18° North (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 23).
Longitudes are east or west, so the answer is 36°E and 43°E. (Option A has the right numbers but the wrong letter N.) Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Eritrea is between 36°E and 43°E longitude.

similar_questions.stem: Eritrea lies between latitudes:
explanation_steps: 12°N and 18°N. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which country occupied Masswa in 1557?
explanation_steps: The Turks (the Ottoman Empire, today's Turkey) occupied Massawa in 1557 (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 71; Grade 8, p. 59). Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: The Turks took Massawa in 1557.

similar_questions.stem: The Italians took over Massawa in:
explanation_steps: February 5, 1885. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Debarwa was the capital of:
explanation_steps: The capital of the Bahri Negastat was at Debarwa (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 69). Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Debarwa was the capital of the Bahri Negestat.

similar_questions.stem: In the 17th century the centre of power moved from Debarwa to:
explanation_steps: Hazzega. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the year 650 C.E?

options.B: the middle of the 7 th century

explanation_steps: The 7th century is from 601 to 700 C.E. (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 13).
650 is in the middle of 601–700. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: 650 C.E. is in the middle of the 7th century.

similar_questions.stem: The year 1210 C.E. is at the beginning of the:
explanation_steps: 1201–1300 is the 13th century. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 2 – Measuring Time, Centuries, p. 13

questions.stem: The record of the past events is called_______________:
explanation_steps: History is the record of past events (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 1–2). Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: History is the story of the past.

similar_questions.stem: The study of the earth and its places is:
explanation_steps: Geography. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 1 – Sources, What is history?, p. 2
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: A period of 100 years is called:
explanation_steps: A century is a period of 100 years (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 9). Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: 100 years is a century.

similar_questions.stem: A millennium is:
explanation_steps: 1000 years. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 2 – Measuring Time, Measuring time, p. 9

questions.stem: The year 450 C.E is in the:
explanation_steps: The 5th century is 401–500 C.E. (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 13).
450 is between 401 and 500. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: 450 C.E. is in the 5th century.

similar_questions.stem: In which century is 99 C.E.?
explanation_steps: 1–100 is the 1st century. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 2 – Measuring Time, Centuries, p. 13

questions.stem: Decline in soil fertility can be improved by:
explanation_steps: The textbook: fertilizers can be used to increase soil fertility (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 26; Grade 8, p. 43). Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Fertilizers make poor soil rich again.

similar_questions.stem: Which practice lets the soil rest and regain fertility?
explanation_steps: Fallowing. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 2 – Population, Population and resources, p. 26
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: A form of settlement which is common in dry climate is:
explanation_steps: The textbook: in dry areas rainfall is not enough for farming; people graze animals, so the settlement is scattered (dispersed) (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 37).
Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: In dry areas houses are far apart. This is dispersed settlement.

similar_questions.stem: Nucleated settlement is common where there is:
explanation_steps: Enough resources bring people together. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 6 – Settlement, Dispersed settlement, p. 37
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of primary economic activity?
explanation_steps: Primary activities take things directly from nature: farming, grazing animals, fishing, mining (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 95–96).
Making furniture and manufacturing are secondary. Driving is a service (tertiary). Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Grazing animals is a primary activity.
tips: Primary = from nature. Secondary = making things. Tertiary = services.

similar_questions.stem: Making furniture is a ___ activity.
explanation_steps: It makes a product. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 11 – Economic Activities, A. Primary activities, p. 95
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which of these statements is <u>correct</u> about the location of Eritrea?

options.A: Eritrea is found south of the equator.
options.B: Eritrea is found to the west of the Red Sea.
options.C: Eritrea is found to the west of Sudan.
options.D: Eritrea has no border with Djibouti.

explanation_steps: Eritrea is between 12°N and 18°N, so it is north of the equator. The Sudan is to its west, and Djibouti is on its south-east (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 23).
The Red Sea is on Eritrea's east, so Eritrea is west of the Red Sea. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: The Red Sea is east of Eritrea, so Eritrea is west of the Red Sea.
tips: Eritrea: north of the equator, east of the Sudan, west of the Red Sea.

similar_questions.stem: Which country is to the west of Eritrea?
explanation_steps: The Sudan. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – The Location and Size of Eritrea

questions.stem: Which of these areas in Eritrea have high population density?
explanation_steps: The textbook: in Eritrea the highlands are more densely populated than the lowlands (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 16). Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: More people live in the highlands.
tips: Highlands: cool, more rain → more people.

similar_questions.stem: Why are the highlands densely populated?
explanation_steps: Good climate for farming. Answer: B.

questions.stem: One of the following increases the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere:

options.B: an increase in use of fossil fuels
options.C: an increase in use of fire wood

explanation_steps: Burning fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas) and burning wood both give out carbon dioxide (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 34).
Afforestation (planting trees) takes carbon dioxide out of the air. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Burning fuel and firewood both add carbon dioxide.
tips: Burning → CO₂ up. Trees → CO₂ down.

similar_questions.stem: Which one reduces carbon dioxide in the air?
explanation_steps: Trees take in CO₂. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 3 – People and the Environment, Global warming, p. 34

questions.stem: Which of these is a cause of global warming?

options.A: increase in the level of sea water
options.C: melting of the polar ice caps

explanation_steps: Global warming is caused by burning fossil fuels, wood and charcoal (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 34).
Rising sea level and melting ice caps are effects (p. 35). Reforestation helps to stop it. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Burning wood and charcoal causes global warming.

similar_questions.stem: Which is an effect of global warming?
explanation_steps: Melting ice is an effect. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 3 – People and the Environment, Global warming, p. 34
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: One of the following is a major reason for the decrease of wild animals in Eritrea.
explanation_steps: The textbook: the number of wild animals has decreased due to droughts, expansion of agriculture and the thirty years of war (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 107).
Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Farms took the land of wild animals.

similar_questions.stem: Which one also reduced wild animals in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: War. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 7 – Natural Heritages, 7.4 Terrestrial vegetation and wild animals, p. 107
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Domestication of animals means:

options.B: keeping and using cattle for human benefit
options.C: keeping wild animals away from cattle

explanation_steps: Early people kept animals around them and used them. This is cattle breeding, or domestication of animals (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 65).
Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Domestication = keeping animals and using them.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a domestic animal?
explanation_steps: Goats live with people. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Grouping of clans is called:
explanation_steps: The textbook: people living close to one another formed clans. Clans joined together to form tribes (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 79). Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Many clans together make a tribe.

similar_questions.stem: People who live close and communicate first formed:
explanation_steps: Clans came first. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> a branch of government?
explanation_steps: The three branches of government are the legislature, the executive and the judiciary (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 85).
Federalism is a system of government, not a branch. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Federalism is a type of government, not a branch.

similar_questions.stem: Which branch judges cases?
explanation_steps: Judiciary. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 6 – Government, Branches of government, p. 85
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which statement <u>is not</u> correct about Mount Soira?

options.B: It is about 3000 meters above sea level
options.C: It is located in Zoba Debub

explanation_steps: The textbook: the altitude of Eritrea rises to over 3000 metres at Mount Soira, the highest point (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 2). It is in the Southern Region (Zoba Debub).
Emba Soira is a volcano that no longer erupts (Grade 7, p. 121). So D is not correct. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Mount Soira is not an active volcano.
tips: Soira: highest, over 3000 m, Zoba Debub, not active.

similar_questions.stem: The lowest place in Eritrea is in the:
explanation_steps: About 120 m below sea level. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which one <u>is not</u> part of surface water?
explanation_steps: Surface water is water on top of the ground: rivers, lakes, seas, oceans, dams and ponds (Social Studies Grade 8, Unit 2).
Wells take water from under the ground. They are groundwater. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Wells use groundwater, not surface water.
tips: Surface = on top. Ground water = under the ground.

similar_questions.stem: Water under the ground is called:
explanation_steps: Groundwater. Answer: B.

questions.stem: What is the reason for the absence of permanent rivers in Eritrea?

options.B: the rivers rise from the highland
options.C: there is rain throughout the year

explanation_steps: The textbook: rainfall in Eritrea is low and irregular and evaporation is high. So there are no permanent rivers; they have water only during the rainy seasons (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 16).
Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Rain comes only in some seasons, so rivers dry up.

similar_questions.stem: The largest and longest river in Eritrea is the:
explanation_steps: The Mereb. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The conflict between the Portuguese and the Turks was caused:

options.A: by their desire to control the region of the Horn
options.B: because of the alliance of the Abyssinian king and the Turks
options.C: because both wanted to control the trade with the East

explanation_steps: The textbook: both the Turks and the Portuguese were interested in the trade with the east. Both wanted to control the region of the Horn (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 74).
The Abyssinian king was friends with the Portuguese, not the Turks, so B is wrong. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Both wanted the Horn and the trade with the East.
tips: Turks vs Portuguese: Horn + eastern trade.

similar_questions.stem: During the Gragn wars, the Abyssinian king asked for help from the:
explanation_steps: The Portuguese. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which one <u>was not</u> a part of the Caste System in India?
explanation_steps: The textbook: the caste system in India had priests, warriors, merchants and farmers, and servants and workers (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 73).
Gods and goddesses are not a group of people. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: The caste system was for people. Gods were not a caste.

similar_questions.stem: In the Indian caste system, the top group was the:
explanation_steps: Priests. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is true</u> about Mahber Fikri Hager?

options.B: It defended the needs of the Italians
options.C: It was an association opposed to colonialism

explanation_steps: The textbook: in 1941 a movement called Mahber Fiqri Hager was formed. It was an anti-colonial association and demanded an end to Italian privileges (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 81). So C is true and B is false.
History books give the founding date as May 5, 1941. So A is also true. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Mahber Fikri Hager was formed in 1941 and was against colonialism.

similar_questions.stem: The first Eritrean political party was:
explanation_steps: The Moslem League (1946). Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 5 – Expansionism and Colonialism, 5.5 Political movements during the British period, p. 81

questions.review_flag: The textbook (G8 p. 81) gives only the year 1941, not the exact date 'May 5, 1941' in option A. D depends on this date (the date usually given in history books). If a teacher does not accept A, then C alone is correct. Same issue as SS 2012 Q30.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs <u>does not</u> match?
explanation_steps: The textbook: the administrative divisions were led by Italian administrators (commissari) (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 92). So commissari were Italians, not Eritreans.
Bandas were Eritrean irregular soldiers, Zaptias were Eritrean military police (p. 95), and the Italians issued Racial Laws in 1937. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Commissari were Italian administrators, not Eritrean.
tips: Commissari = Italian. Ascari, Bandas, Zaptias = Eritrean.

similar_questions.stem: The Racial Laws were introduced by the Italians in:
explanation_steps: 1937. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 6 – Colonial Administrations in Eritrea, Italian colonial administration, p. 92
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Deggiat Hailu of Tseazzega was defeated by Ras Woldemichael at the Battle of:
explanation_steps: The textbook: Raesi Woldemichael fought against Hailu of Tseazzega at the Battle of Wokki Duba (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 73). Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Woldemichael defeated Hailu at Wokki Duba.

similar_questions.stem: Degiat Bahta Hagos was killed at the Battle of:
explanation_steps: Halay, 1894. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 5 – Expansionism and Colonialism, Abyssinian expansion – Raesi Woldemichael, p. 73

questions.stem: Which of the following is an effect of deforestation?
explanation_steps: When trees are cut, rain and wind carry the soil away. Trees help prevent soil erosion (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 84).
Crop rotation, terracing and fallowing are ways to protect soil. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Cutting trees causes soil erosion.

similar_questions.stem: Which method reduces soil erosion on slopes?
explanation_steps: Terracing. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 10 – Natural Resources and Conservation, Forests and soil, p. 84
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Eritrea was federated with Ethiopia by:
explanation_steps: The textbook: on December 2, 1950, through Resolution 390A (V), the UN General Assembly decided to join Eritrea with Ethiopia in a Federation (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 83).
Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: UN Resolution 390A(V) made the federation.

similar_questions.stem: The Federation started on:
explanation_steps: September 11, 1952. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 5 – Expansionism and Colonialism, The question of Eritrea's future, p. 83

questions.stem: The final defeat of the Egyptians took place at the Battle of:
explanation_steps: The textbook: the Egyptians were defeated at Gundet in 1875 and again at Gura in 1876. After Gura they were driven out of the highlands (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 68).
Dogalli (1887) was a defeat of the Italians. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: The Egyptians were finally defeated at Gura (1876).

similar_questions.stem: The Egyptians were first defeated in the highlands at:
explanation_steps: Gundet, 1875. Answer: B.

questions.stem: In Eritrea fishing is:

options.A: the main economic activity of the island population
options.B: the main source of domestic income
options.C: the main source of food for the majority of the people

explanation_steps: The textbook: because of the many marine animals, the main economic activity of the people of the coastal areas and islands is fishing (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 140).
For the whole country, agriculture is the main activity. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: People on the islands live mainly by fishing.
tips: Islands and coast = fishing. Whole country = farming.

similar_questions.stem: Fish is also an important ___ item of Eritrea.
explanation_steps: Fish is exported. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of these crops is different from the others?
explanation_steps: Chick pea, broad beans and lentils are pulses (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 132).
Cotton is a fibre crop (p. 135). Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Cotton is a fibre crop. The others are pulses.
tips: Pulses: chick pea, beans, lentils, peas.

similar_questions.stem: Which is an oil seed?
explanation_steps: Sesame. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following events comes <u>first</u>?

options.B: Buying of Assab by Giuseppe Sapeto

explanation_steps: Dates: Sapeto bought Assab in 1869; Battle of Dogalli 1887; Italian colony declared January 1, 1890; annexation by Ethiopia 1962 (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 74–76).
The earliest is 1869. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Sapeto bought Assab first, in 1869.

similar_questions.stem: The Italian colony of Eritrea was declared in:
explanation_steps: January 1, 1890. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 5 – Expansionism and Colonialism, Buying of Assab, p. 74
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which of the following events comes <u>last</u>?
explanation_steps: Dates: Resolution 390A(V) 1950; Battle of Afabet March 1988; Operation Fenkil February 1990; liberation of Eritrea May 24, 1991 (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 83, 113).
The latest is liberation in 1991. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Liberation (1991) came last.

similar_questions.stem: Operation Fenkil (1990) freed:
explanation_steps: Massawa. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 7 – Highlights of the Eritrean Armed Struggle, Military developments, p. 113
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 7 – Highlights of the Eritrean Armed Struggle

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of modern industry?

options.D: The gold smiths in the towns

explanation_steps: Modern industries use machines in factories, for example Asmara Textile and shoe factories (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 145–148; Grade 6, p. 97).
Pottery, basketry and goldsmith work are traditional handicrafts. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: A shoe factory is modern industry.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a traditional handicraft?
explanation_steps: Basketry. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 9 – Economic Activities in Eritrea, Industry, p. 145
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: How many decades are there between the start of the Eritrean Armed struggle (1961) and the Liberation of Eritrea (1991) ?
explanation_steps: A decade is 10 years (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 9). 30 ÷ 10 = 3 decades. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: 30 years is 3 decades.

similar_questions.stem: How many decades are there in 50 years?
explanation_steps: 50 ÷ 10 = 5. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 2 – Measuring Time, Measuring time, p. 9
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which of the following events comes <u>first</u>?
explanation_steps: Dates: Federation began September 11, 1952; Battle of Afabet 1988; declaration of independence May 24, 1993; constitution ratified May 23, 1997 (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 106, 113, 117, 120).
The earliest is 1952. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: The Federation (1952) came first.

similar_questions.stem: The Eritrean Constitution was ratified in:
explanation_steps: May 23, 1997. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 6 – Colonial Administrations in Eritrea, Federation, p. 106
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Figure 1 below shows the map of an area. If the map distance between town A and town B along the road is 8cm find the ground distance between the two towns (A-B) in kilometers.
questions.image_alt: Figure 1: a map with town A (lower left) and town B (upper right) joined by a road. Scale: 1 cm to 2 km.
explanation_steps: Scale: 1 cm to 2 km. Ground distance = map distance × 2 km (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 16–18).
8 cm × 2 km = 16 km. Answer: D.
tips: Multiply the map distance by the scale.

similar_questions.stem: Scale 1 cm to 3 km. Map distance 5 cm. Ground distance =
explanation_steps: 5 × 3 = 15. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 3 – Distance and Scale, Scale statement, p. 16
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: The struggle between the Bahri Negassi and the Turks was caused by:

options.A: Friendship of the Turks with the Abyssinian kings
options.B: Turkish desire to control the Red Sea trade routes
options.C: Friendship of the Portuguese and the Turks

explanation_steps: The Turks wanted to control the Red Sea coast and the route of the trade with the east, so they tried to conquer the land of the Bahri Negestat (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 71–74).
The Turks were enemies of the Portuguese and of the Abyssinian king, so A and C are wrong. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: The Turks wanted the Red Sea trade routes.
tips: Turks = wanted the Red Sea coast and trade.

similar_questions.stem: The Bahri Negash who fought the Turks in the 16th century was:
explanation_steps: Bahri Negash Yeshaq (Isaq). Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 6 textbook – Unit 9 – The Period of the Bahri Negestat, 9.3 Portuguese-Turkish rivalry – summary, p. 74
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 9 – The Period of the Bahri Negestat

questions.stem: Figure 2 below shows the floor plan (floor map) drawn using a scale. If the length of a classroom is 6 meters and its width is 4 meters what is the scale of the plan (map)?
questions.image_alt: Figure 2: a rectangle (floor plan) 3 cm long and 2 cm wide.
explanation_steps: On the plan the length is 3 cm and the width is 2 cm.
3 cm = 6 m, so 1 cm = 2 m. Check: 2 cm × 2 = 4 m. Correct (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 3). Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: 3 cm shows 6 m, so 1 cm shows 2 m.

similar_questions.stem: A room 10 m long is drawn 5 cm long. The scale is:
explanation_steps: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 m per cm. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 7 textbook – Unit 1 – Scale and Measuring Distance, Drawing plans to scale, p. 3
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which factor <u>did not</u> help Italian expansion in Eritrea?

options.A: Eritreans were fed up from Abyssinian attacks
options.B: Eritreans were weakened by the Great Famine
options.D: French support to Italian expansion in Eritrea.

explanation_steps: The textbook: Italian expansion was helped by (1) people being tired of Abyssinian attacks, (2) the Great Famine, and (3) British encouragement (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 75).
France was a rival power; the British encouraged Italy so that France would not take more coast (p. 74). Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: France did not help Italy. Britain did.
tips: Helped Italy: tiredness of attacks, famine, Britain.

similar_questions.stem: The French acquired the port of:
explanation_steps: Djibouti. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 5 – Expansionism and Colonialism, Expansion to the interior, p. 75
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which of these events comes <u>first</u>?
explanation_steps: Dates: referendum 23–25 April 1993; declaration of independence May 24, 1993; National Service 1994; Boundary Commission decision April 2002 (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 117–121).
The referendum came first. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: The referendum (April 1993) came before the declaration (May 1993).
tips: Referendum first, then independence was declared.

similar_questions.stem: The Boundary Commission said Badme belongs to:
explanation_steps: Eritrea (2002). Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Social Studies Grade 8 textbook – Unit 8 – Post-Independence Development, 8.1 The Referendum, p. 117
textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Evaporation is shown by number ______:
questions.image_alt: Figure 3: four drawings of the water cycle. 2 = wavy arrows going up from a water surface. 1 = a cloud with rain falling. 3 = wavy arrows going up from trees and plants. 4 = rivers flowing into the sea.
explanation_steps: Evaporation is water turning into vapour and going up from seas, lakes and rivers.
In drawing 2, wavy arrows go up from a water surface. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Drawing 2 shows water going up from the water. That is evaporation.
tips: Evaporation = from water. Transpiration = from plants.

similar_questions.stem: Water vapour turning into clouds is called:
explanation_steps: Condensation. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Precipitation is shown by number ______:
questions.image_alt: Figure 3: four drawings of the water cycle. 2 = wavy arrows going up from a water surface. 1 = a cloud with rain falling. 3 = wavy arrows going up from trees and plants. 4 = rivers flowing into the sea.
explanation_steps: Precipitation is water falling from clouds as rain, snow or hail.
Drawing 1 shows a cloud with rain falling. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Drawing 1 shows rain. Rain is precipitation.

similar_questions.stem: In Figure 3, which drawing shows rivers flowing to the sea (run-off)?
explanation_steps: Drawing 4. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Transpiration is shown by number ______:
questions.image_alt: Figure 3: four drawings of the water cycle. 2 = wavy arrows going up from a water surface. 1 = a cloud with rain falling. 3 = wavy arrows going up from trees and plants. 4 = rivers flowing into the sea.
explanation_steps: Transpiration is water vapour given out by plants (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 23).
Drawing 3 shows wavy arrows going up from trees and plants. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Drawing 3 shows water going up from plants. That is transpiration.

similar_questions.stem: Water that sinks into the soil is called:
explanation_steps: It seeps into the ground. Answer: A.

passages.title: Figure 3 – The water cycle (Questions 48 to 50)
passages.instructions: In Figure 3, drawings 1, 2, 3, and 4 show different parts of the water cycle. Answer questions 48 to 50 based on the information given.
paragraphs: Figure 3 has four drawings. Drawing 2: wavy arrows go up from a water surface. Drawing 1: a cloud with rain falling. Drawing 3: wavy arrows go up from trees and plants. Drawing 4: rivers flowing into the sea.
